quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: Before getting on a motorcycle, which of the following do you NOT need to check?
questions.correctAnswerText: Paint damage.
questions.explanation: Before getting on a motorcycle, check the tire tread and air pressure, oil and fluid levels, lights, and signals.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: No jacket if it is warm out.
A jacket at all times, even in warm weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: A jacket at all times, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket for protection, even in warm weather. It helps prevent injury and dehydration. Also wear long pants and tuck in shoelaces so they do not catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: The one that lets you travel fastest.
The one that lets you draft off other vehicles.
The one where other drivers can see you.
The one in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: The one where other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and be seen. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It lets you see far to the sides for safe riding.
It does not have a chin strap.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets you see far to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet will not limit your vision. It allows you to see as far as needed for safe riding.

questions.question: What is the correct body position on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit forward with your arms slightly bent on the grips.
Sit far back and stretch to reach the grips.
Lean forward and use your arms to hold yourself up.
Keep your knees far from the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward with your arms slightly bent on the grips.
questions.explanation: Sit far enough forward that your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips. This lets you easily and comfortably reach and use the controls.

questions.question: For the best protection, what type of helmet should you wear?

options.text: One that is well-worn and broken in.

questions.correctAnswerText: One that fits snugly.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no obvious damage.

questions.question: Why should motorcycle riders turn their heads to look over their shoulders before changing lanes?

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles.
It catches the attention of other drivers.
To make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check for vehicles or hazards in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Shifting into a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear slows your motorcycle, similar to braking. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: What happens when you take a corner too fast?

options.text: You may cross into another lane.
It is better than going too slowly.
It is okay because motorcycles are small.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast can cause you to cross into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before turning or entering a curve.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Braking.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have a manual transmission. Downshifting to a lower gear slows you down.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Shift through multiple gears at once.
Shift through one gear at a time.
Always shift all the way to neutral first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift through one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: Shift down one gear at a time. Let out the clutch slowly through each downshift.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. Small problems on a motorcycle can be more dangerous than on a car.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.

questions.question: What must a passenger be able to do?

options.text: Reach the footrests with both feet.
Completely wrap their arms around the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reach the footrests with both feet.
questions.explanation: A passenger must be able to reach the footrests on both sides of the motorcycle with both feet while sitting. The motorcycle must be designed to safely carry a passenger.

questions.question: Why are signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They serve little purpose since motorcycles are small.
They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
You should not use them if no vehicles are nearby.
They are more complicated than car signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: They alert other drivers to what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Use turn signals to tell others about your plans. Always use them when you change lanes or turn, even if you think no one else is nearby.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep going and hope to wake up.
Get off the road and rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off the road and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride if you are tired. On long trips, take a rest break at least every two hours to avoid fatigue.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The more it builds up in your body.
The faster your body removes it.
The less it will affect you.
The more likely you will avoid being pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: The more it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the more alcohol builds up in your body. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT required on a legal motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: A flag.
questions.explanation: In Minnesota, motorcycles must have a rearview mirror, a horn, a muffler, at least one headlight, a red taillight, and at least one brake. If the motorcycle has a passenger seat, it must also have footrests.

questions.question: Which of the following should NOT be checked before every ride?
questions.correctAnswerText: The seat fabric.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check the spokes and rims for damage, check tire tread and condition, and check all lights.

questions.question: What does long-term wind noise exposure while riding do?

options.text: Is less harmful than listening to music.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause hearing loss.
questions.explanation: Wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear proper hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if garments are very loose and flap in the wind.
Yes, if pants and a jacket cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if pants and a jacket cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Good clothing reduces crash injuries. Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs. They should be made of sturdy material and fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Hide your intentions from other drivers.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see better and be seen better.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see better and be seen better.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see others and lets them see you. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Can greatly reduce head injury severity.
Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can greatly reduce head injury severity.
questions.explanation: Wearing a DOT-approved helmet greatly protects your head and neck in a crash. A good helmet will not limit your side vision.

questions.question: Which color is best for being seen while riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Orange
questions.explanation: Orange, red, yellow, and green clothing make you easier to see. Wear bright colors at all times while riding, day or night.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Are not helpful since you can't do anything about what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of regular scanning. Also check mirrors before changing lanes, stopping at an intersection, or slowing down.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes in both the front and rear.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes in both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes—one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should:

options.text: Not be worn during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn at night.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials to be more visible, especially at night. Bright colors with reflective materials make you easier to see for other drivers.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket or pants, look for:
questions.correctAnswerText: Items made of leather.
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs. Leather provides the best protection.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white background and black lettering. Riders must follow all rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: Switching to a lower gear is also called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Engine braking.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear slows your motorcycle like braking does. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: What does a face shield do?

options.text: Does not protect the face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects the eyes and face.
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield gives the best protection for your eyes and face. Eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough protection. In Vermont, you do not need eye or face protection if your motorcycle has a windshield, but it is still recommended.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Left turn
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or along with turn signals. When you extend your left arm straight out to the left, it means you plan to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT protect a motorcycle rider?

options.text: Boots that go over the ankle
A baseball cap that fits snugly

questions.correctAnswerText: A baseball cap that fits snugly
questions.explanation: To stay safe, wear a DOT-compliant helmet, face or eye protection, a sturdy jacket and long pants, high boots or shoes that support your ankles, and gloves made of durable material.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks does the body eliminate per hour?
questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: The body can eliminate about one drink per hour on average. The time needed to lower your blood alcohol level varies. It is safest not to drive any vehicle after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist constantly watch for ahead on the road?
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead for changing traffic, dangerous road conditions, and escape routes. Stay ready to react to any changes.

questions.question: The front brake is:

options.text: Only to be used if the rear brake fails.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safe if used properly.
questions.explanation: The front brake is safe when used correctly. It is more powerful than the rear brake and provides at least three-fourths of the total stopping power.

questions.question: When checking tires before riding, what should you NOT look at?
questions.correctAnswerText: Shininess
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet has all of these EXCEPT:

options.text: Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap retention system.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle operator should be ready for:

options.text: A car to suddenly pull out of a parking space into traffic.
Other drivers to see the motorcycle and stay out of its way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car to suddenly pull out of a parking space into traffic.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, be ready for one to suddenly pull out into traffic. It is often safest to ride in the left part of your lane when parked cars are on your right. This gives you more space between your motorcycle and any dangers.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Equip and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
Ride as you would without a passenger.
Make sure footrests are only for you, the operator.
Teach the passenger after you start riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Equip and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Only carry a passenger if your motorcycle is properly equipped and adjusted for one. Your motorcycle should have separate footrests for the passenger and a seat large enough for two people to sit comfortably. You may need to adjust your headlight, tire pressure, and suspension for the extra weight.
